short: A disastrous English naval expedition that failed to exploit the Spanish Armada's defeat.
full:
Launched in April 1589, the English Armada was a massive naval expedition commanded by Sir Francis Drake and Sir John Norreys. Following the defeat of the Spanish Armada the previous year, Queen Elizabeth I sought to press her advantage by destroying the surviving Spanish Atlantic fleet, instigating a revolt in Portugal, and intercepting the Spanish treasure fleet at the Azores.

The campaign was a resounding failure, plagued by poor planning, inadequate supplies, and tactical blunders. An attack on A Coruña failed to destroy the main Spanish fleet and instead resulted in heavy English casualties. Subsequent operations in Lisbon were similarly disastrous, as the expected Portuguese uprising never materialized and disease devastated the English troops. The fleet returned to England in July having lost thousands of men and numerous ships, severely damaging Drake's reputation and allowing Spain to rapidly rebuild its naval supremacy for the remainder of the war.
